reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the redline grants a strong licence back but never states in operative language that SFJ owns only generic tools (and correspondingly that Customer-side data/deliverable rights are otherwise preserved), so the ownership allocation half of the fallback bargain is missing.

The licence grant itself hits every required attribute (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense) and its "for any and all purposes" scope covers business use, plus survival on termination.

Preferred level is not reached: SFJ remains sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package and Research Results until the Exhibit K purchase, with no assignment, no pre-existing IP/embedded IP construct and no express Customer Data retention or no-joint-ownership statement.

Minimality fails on a few unnecessary additions beyond what the fallback requires — "fully-paid", "non-exclusive", and the expanded verb string "reproduce, disclose and otherwise exploit" — although the survival sentence is defensible as making "perpetual" effective.
Intent is preserved: the purchase/payment construct, confidentiality deeming provisions and definitions are untouched, and no undefined term or contradiction is introduced.
